title: Record the DPDP breach-assessment decision for the plaintext credential exposure
description: Using the outputs of tasks 4 and 5, assess whether plaintext storage of Zerodha/Binance credentials in the db-models collections (metastore classification restricted/spdi) or disclosure through MCP transcripts and dry-run logs amounts to a personal data breach under dpdp-rules-2025 (security safeguards rule 6(1)(a)/(b)). Decide whether breach notification under rule 7 is required: it is required only if there is evidence of unauthorised access, and if so its 72-hour clock runs from awareness. Record the decision, the evidence considered and the reasoning as a soc ledger observation (methods document-review, controlIds sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S1 and dpdp-rules-2025:6(1)(a)) handed to soc-ledger-keeper. Coordinate with the CISO on the parallel CERT-In/SEBI 6-hour incident-reporting assessment if unauthorised access is found.
acceptanceCriteria: A soc ledger observation exists in company-profile/example-co/soc/main.jsonl with methods document-review, citing dpdp-rules-2025 6(1)(a), that states whether a notifiable personal data breach occurred and references the task 4 and task 5 evidence

If the decision is notifiable, an incident record with regulatorReportRefs for MeitY (72 h) and CERT-In/SEBI (6 h) exists; if not, the observation states the absence of evidence of unauthorised access that supports that conclusion

verificationMethod.description: The DPO signs off on the breach-assessment observation, and the CISO countersigns it in the task evidence. Expected result: a dated, signed decision linked to the ledger observation id, plus an incident id when notification is required.

rootCause.description: Plaintext credential handling in code left personal and financial account credentials without DPDP rule 6 safeguards, so the organisation must determine whether the exposure window created a reportable breach.
